title: EMA10/50 crossover entry, switchable auto-lot (balance-scaled) or martingale x2
entry_long: EMA10 crosses above EMA50 (exponential), 1 order per bar (Once per Bar filter)
entry_short: EMA10 crosses below EMA50 (exponential), 1 order per bar
escalation_cap: none stated (doubles 0.1->0.2->0.4... on each loss, resets to 0.1 on win; no max-step cap mentioned)
buildon_idea: add explicit step cap (e.g. 4-5 doublings) or switch to linear-add lot law; the built-in auto-lot mode (lot = balance/100000) is itself a safer alternative already present in the EA - test that branch flat first
novelty_note: simple 2-EMA cross, boolean switch lets user pick balance-scaled fixed lot vs martingale; low novelty mechanism, teaching example for switch-block usage

title: EMA10/50 crossover entry, switchable auto-lot (balance-scaled) or martingale x2 (English narration, same example as EX001)
entry_long: EMA_Fast(10) above EMA_Trend(200) context + EMA_Fast crosses above EMA_slow(50), exponential, candle ID1
entry_short: mirror: EMA_Fast crosses below EMA_slow, exponential, candle ID1
escalation_cap: none stated (0.1->0.2->0.4->0.8->1.6 shown as example progression, no explicit ceiling); auto-lot alt mode = balance/100000
buildon_idea: add explicit step cap or switch to linear-add; backtest showed martingale mode 100%+ profit/21% DD on 1yr @$1000 vs auto-lot mode 39% profit/17.9% DD on 1yr @$20000 - test both modes flat-lot before trusting the martingale number (small-account result likely overfit to few paths)
novelty_note: same mechanism as EX001/JQ90QIo7wBM, English re-narration adds EMA200 trend constant not used in the Thai version's stated conditions; low novelty

title: Auto trend-line breakout (highest/lowest price over 50 vs 15 candle lookback) with martingale x2
entry_long: highest price of last 50 candles > highest price of last 15 candles -> draw green trendline; buy when candle close ID1 crosses above the trendline
entry_short: lowest price of last 50 candles < lowest price of last 15 candles -> draw red trendline; sell when candle close ID1 crosses below the trendline
escalation_cap: none stated (doubles 0.1->0.2->0.4... on loss, resets on win; open/close order switch defaults False until enabled)
buildon_idea: add step cap on the martingale ladder; the auto-trendline (highest/lowest price over configurable lookback) is a reusable breakout-detection block worth extracting into EDGE_CATALOG regardless of the martingale lot law; 2yr backtest showed 200%+ profit/34.4% DD @$10000 on EURUSD-style test - re-verify flat-lot before trusting
novelty_note: auto-drawn trendline via 2 reference points (50-candle high/low vs 15-candle high/low) is a distinctive breakout-detection technique; medium novelty

title: Bollinger Band mean-reversion entry + engulfing filter, distance-based auto lot-doubling grid add-on
entry_long: candle ID1 & ID2 low both below BB lower band (bullish reversal candles, min body 5 pip) -> buy 0.1 fixed lot, no SL/TP; subsequent adds when price keeps falling: if gap from last buy >=50 pip use lot x2 (needs bullish reversal candle re-crossing BB lower band), else re-add at fixed 0.1 lot
entry_short: mirror: candle ID1 & ID2 high both above BB upper band -> sell 0.1 fixed lot; adds mirror the buy-side grid/lot-doubling logic
exit: close all buy+sell when combined profit > 10 pip (single position) or > 5 pip (2+ positions), no fixed SL/TP
escalation_cap: none stated (lot doubles via formula lot_BS*2 on adds spaced >=50 pip; no max order count or lot ceiling mentioned)
buildon_idea: add no_sl -> hard SL and a max-orders cap on the grid; distance-gated lot-doubling (only escalate lot if the adverse move exceeds 50 pip) is a more disciplined grid variant than plain martingale - worth extracting as reusable pattern; 2yr backtest showed 43.19% profit/17.52% DD @$10000, 725 trades - re-test with SL added since current no-SL exposure is unbounded on gap risk
novelty_note: BB band-touch reversal entry + a spacing-gated lot-escalation rule (not pure time/loss-triggered martingale) is a somewhat novel grid variant

title: Equity-drawdown-controlled EMA12/20 crossover: fixed lot normally, escalating lot when equity drops below a rolling 5%-of-equity floor
entry_long: EMA12 crosses above EMA20 (candle ID2) and EMA12 stays above EMA20 by >3 pip distance (candle ID0), exponential; first order = 0.1 fixed lot, no SL/TP
entry_short: mirror: EMA12 crosses below EMA20 by >3 pip distance
exit: close all buy+sell when combined profit > $30; also an equity-floor recompute (equity - 5% of equity) after every order
escalation_cap: none stated (lot doubles via lot_BS*2 each additional order placed only while equity stays below the rolling floor; resets to 0 after the $30 profit close)
buildon_idea: add hard SL and an explicit max-order cap; the equity-floor trigger (only escalate lot once equity has already dropped 5% from last-recorded high) is a distinctive drawdown-gated martingale variant worth extracting - it only doubles lot after confirmed adverse equity movement, not blindly on every loss; 2yr backtest showed 12.9% max DD @$10000, 81 trades - relatively tame result worth re-verifying flat-lot
novelty_note: equity-percentage floor as the martingale trigger (instead of simple consecutive-loss counting) is a notable risk-aware twist on martingale; medium-high novelty

title: 6-candle reversal pattern (3 candles one direction + 3 opposite) fixed-lot entry, no SL/TP, pip-target close
entry_long: ID1,ID2,ID3 bullish (min body 2 pip) followed by ID4,ID5,ID6 bearish (min body 2 pip) -> buy 0.1 fixed lot, no SL/TP
entry_short: mirror: ID1,ID2,ID3 bearish followed by ID4,ID5,ID6 bullish -> sell 0.1 fixed lot
exit: close all buy+sell when combined profit > 15 pip; no SL/TP
buildon_idea: no martingale here, but no_sl is the key risk to fix - add a hard SL; author's own follow-up (2023 test on same config) showed the strategy breaking down (max DD 59.57% vs 27.99% in 2022) which is the classic single-year overfit trap this lab's VERDICT GATE already guards against - re-test across both trend and recent-year windows before any verdict
novelty_note: straightforward 6-candle up-then-down (or down-then-up) reversal count pattern; low-medium novelty, simple and explainable

title: Spinning-top candlestick reversal (long wicks both sides, small body) entry with martingale x2 and fixed SL/TP
entry_long: ID1 bullish with both upper & lower wick > body size, ID2 & ID3 bearish (min body 4 pip) -> buy at ID0 open, martingale lot (init 0.1, x2 on loss)
entry_short: mirror: ID1 bearish with both wicks > body size, ID2 & ID3 bullish -> sell at ID0 open, martingale lot
escalation_cap: none stated (x2 on loss, no max-step cap)
buildon_idea: add explicit step cap; author's own cross-year test is the key finding here - 2022 alone showed 86% profit/34.2% DD @$1000, but 2023 alone on the SAME config blew up to -835 loss/92.2% DD @$1000 (fixed by raising capital to $10000, which cut profit to only 23.7% over 2yrs) - textbook proof that martingale needs both capital sizing AND regime-robustness checked together, exactly the lab's Both-regimes gate rule
novelty_note: spinning-top (long wicks, small body) reversal filter distinct from EX005's body-based reversal; low-medium novelty

title: Combined reversal(EX005-style 6-candle) + spinning-top(EX006-style) entries in parallel groups, martingale lot, pooled profit-target close, optional equity%% cut-loss switch
entry_long: group1 (spinning-top): ID1 bullish w/ both wicks>body, ID2&ID3 bearish min body 4pip; group2 (reversal): ID1,ID2,ID3 bullish min body 2pip + ID4,ID5,ID6 bearish min body 2pip -> buy martingale lot (init 0.1, x2 on loss), no SL/TP, tagged by group 1 or 2
entry_short: mirror conditions for both groups -> sell martingale lot, no SL/TP
exit: close all (both groups) when pooled profit > $100; optional Cut_loss_Mode switch (default off) closes all if pooled loss < -30% of balance
escalation_cap: none stated on the martingale ladder itself; only account-level circuit breaker is the optional -30%-of-balance cut-loss (off by default)
buildon_idea: turn the optional Cut_loss_Mode ON by default and add per-order SL, not just an account-level -30% breaker; combining two independent pattern families (spinning-top + 6-candle reversal) into shared risk pooling is itself the buildable idea - it increased 2yr profit to 90.76% while cutting max DD to 27.19% (vs EX005/EX006 standalone, which blew up in the 2023-alone test) - worth extracting as a portfolio-pooling pattern even before fixing the martingale/no-SL issues
novelty_note: multi-signal pooling with shared profit-target and shared optional equity-based circuit breaker is a notable structural idea (diversification-via-pooling), even though each individual signal is low-novelty

title: Double-Hammer reversal (2 candles, long lower/upper wick, small body) with EMA100 trend filter and martingale x2
entry_long: price below EMA100 (trend filter) + Double Hammer: ID1 & ID2 lower wick > upper wick, and ID1 body < ID1 upper wick -> buy martingale lot (init 0.1, x2 on loss)
entry_short: mirror: price above EMA100 + inverse Double Hammer (upper wick > lower wick both candles, ID1 body < ID1 lower wick) -> sell martingale lot
escalation_cap: none stated (x2 on loss via lot_martingale constant, no max-step cap)
buildon_idea: add explicit step cap or switch to linear-add; the EMA100 trend filter (only take Hammer reversals against the EMA, i.e. counter-trend at a level) is a distinct filter worth testing standalone vs the bare pattern in EX005/EX006/EX007; narrator ran a from-2022-to-present control-point backtest and called it 'works well' with no numeric report shown - re-verify with actual metrics before trusting
novelty_note: double-hammer (2-candle wick pattern) plus an EMA200-alternative trend filter (EMA100) not used in the other candlestick-pattern examples; medium novelty via the trend-filter addition
